newsitem.title: USA: Impaired U.S. driver gets life term, no parole.
newsitem.headline: Impaired U.S. driver gets life term, no parole.

text.p: A North Carolina man convicted of first-degree murder for killing two women while driving under the influence of beer and painkillers was sentenced to life in prison without parole on Tuesday.

A jury deliberated for about 70 minutes before making the recommendation in the case of Thomas Richard Jones, 39, who was found guilty in the deaths of Julie Hansen and Maia Witzl, two 19-year-old students at Wake Forest University.
The judge immediately imposed the sentence. Jones was the first person in North Carolina to be convicted of first-degree murder for causing traffic deaths.
Prosecutors had sought the death penalty for Jones, a move that was thought to be unprecedented in an impaired driving case in the United States.
"It's a national precedent just to get life without parole," Prosecutor Vincent Rabil said.

Jones's court-appointed defence attorneys, Carol Teeter and David Freedman, said they would appeal and thought the conviction would be overturned because the court had gone too far in applying state law.

Witnesses at the trial said Jones, who had a record of impaired driving convictions, was high on painkillers and beer when he veered his car into an oncoming vehicle on Sept. 4. Hansen and Witzl were killed and four others were injured.
Jones, who lost part of his leg in a lawn mower accident 16 years ago, said he had led a life of alcoholism and drug dependency.
The parents of the slain women said they were satisfied with the verdict.
Jones's wife sat quietly in the courtroom during the trial and refused any comment to the press.
